  FINISHED AGENDA & MINUTES

CALL TO ORDER

Chair Julie Lie called the meeting to order at 4:03 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present: Bedy, Chotiswatdi, Hilliard, Howat, Killion, Noble, Russell, Scott,
  Wood, Lie

Also present: Paul Duncan, Homeless Services Bureau Manager, Jennifer Santana, Community
Program Specialist, Joseph Botelho, Attendee.

Roll call taken by Jennifer Santana.

REGULAR AGENDA

1.  26-54144  Recommendation to approve the minutes for the Homeless Services Advisory

  A motion was made by Member Bedy, seconded by Member Wood, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  9  Lie, Wood, Scott, Russell, Noble, Killion, Howat, Hilliard, Bedy
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 1  Chotiswatdi

2.  26-57043  Recommendation to receive and file updates from the Mayor’s Fund and Policy
  Subcommittee and the Continuum of Care (CoC) Homeless Services Advisory
  Committee (HSAC) representative.

  Mayor's Fund Subcommittee
  • Member Jim Howat provided an update regarding the last Mayor's Fund
  Meeting.
  • Committee members are concerned with fundraising strategies.
  • The subcommittee would also like to consider funding a pilot program using
  the Mayor's Fund.
  Policy Subcommittee
  • Member Sarah Bedy provided an update on the last policy meeting,
  discussion included member and council conversations regarding the policy
  recommendations.
  • The subcommittee discussed cost effective Homeless Service models. They
  are looking to find the top service needs including sanitation services that will
  meet the needs of those experiencing homelessness.
  • Members of the committee suggested that the subcommittee work on
  presenting a budget for this project.
  CoC Updates
  • Member Patricia Scott provided an update regarding the Long Beach CoC.
  The board met on Tuesday, February 3, 2026 to discuss the CoC Program
  Notice of Funding (NOFO).
  • Staff recommendation to the board Pathway #1, projects funded in FY 2024
  are not reallocated, replaced, or consolidated, may be eligible for FY
  2025selection using the FY 2024 submission with written confirmation from
  collaborative applicant. This will be submitted to HUD next week Monday,
  February 9, 2026.

3.  26-57272  Recommendation to receive and file updates on committee members’ meetings
  with their respective council members concerning the 2025 Policy
  Recommendations.

  A motion was made by Member Killion, seconded by Member Scott, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  10 Lie, Wood, Scott, Russell, Noble, Killion, Howat, Hilliard, Chotiswatdi,
  Bedy

  • Members of the committee provided a brief update based on their
  discussions with their respective council members.
  • Members that have not yet met with their council members to discuss the
  Policy recommendations will have an opportunity to share at the next
  scheduled meeting.

4.  26-57047  Recommendation to receive and file the Homeless Services Bureau Staff
  Operations and Updates Report from the Health Department.

  A motion was made by Member Wood, seconded by Member Killion, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  10 Lie, Wood, Scott, Russell, Noble, Killion, Howat, Hilliard, Chotiswatdi,
  Bedy
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 0 None

  • Bureau Manager Paul Duncan provided staff and operational updates. The
  bureau is currently undergoing interviews for two internal positions.
  • On December 23, 2025 HUD released and update on the FY 2025 NOFO.
  Staff recommendation to the board Pathway #1, projects funded in FY 2024
  are not reallocated, replaced, or consolidated, may be eligible for FY 2025
  selection using the FY 2024 submission with written confirmation from
  collaborative applicant. This will be submitted to HUD next week Monday,
  February 9, 2026.
  • Member Pam Chotiswatdsi joins the meeting at 4:15 p.m.
  • Project Homekey 5950 Long Beach Blvd has completed construction and
  has begun operations with 78 new units, 20 units have been prioritized for
  state focus along the LA Riverbed. Members have questions regarding units
  and occupant policies.
  • Staff are moving forward on a recommendation for motel lease for the
  Encampment resolution 3 focused on the LA Riverbed, taking this to council
  March 2026.
  • The city began inclement weather shelter (IWS) program at the MSC in
  Novemeber.
  • Due to unforeseen draining issues at the Youth Navigation Center the city is
  working with Public Works to have the sewer pipes re-sloped to prevent

  provide day-to-day operations.
  • Staff are working to develop a homeless prevention rental assistance

  • Shout out to the staff and volunteers that participated in the Point in Time
